description:
Route-level A/B testing framework is a Console-first feature that lets customers split production traffic for a specific API route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions for a given project) across two (or more) model variants and/or configurations, while automatically collecting measurement hooks for latency, cost (token and GPU attribution), error rates, and optional quality signals (offline eval scores and/or sampled human/LLM-judge scoring). The project extends Redwood Inference’s existing rollout primitives (canaries, model pinning, fallback routing) with deterministic assignment, statistically sound experiment reporting, and safe operational guardrails.

Goals:
- Enable customers to define A/B experiments at the route level in Console, with clear traffic allocation controls (e.g., 90/10, 50/50), eligibility rules (tenant/project/region), and start/stop scheduling.
- Provide reliable measurement hooks: p50/p95/p99 latency, time-to-first-token, token counts, per-request cost attribution, error/timeout rates, and experiment exposure logging.
- Integrate optional quality measurement: attach eval suites/prompt sets and compare variant performance using Redwood’s eval harness; support sampled online evaluation pipelines where applicable.
- Deliver a safe operations model: audit logs, rollback workflows, guardrails on metric regressions, and SRE/observability readiness (dashboards/alerts).

Non-goals (initial release):
- Multi-armed bandits / fully automated optimization.
- Arbitrary user-defined metrics ingestion (beyond the standardized hooks).
- Client-side SDK experimentation helpers (beyond documentation/examples).

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (Rollout policies/telemetry requirements).
- Engineering (Console/Platform/Routing): Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Ethan Park, Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Jordan Lee.
- Telemetry/Analytics: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman.
- Applied ML/Evals: Jonas Weber, Olivia Grant, Sana Farid.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Miles Thornton.
- Design: Tessa Morgan, Kenji Nakamura.
- Security: (consulted) audit logging + access controls for experiment configuration.

Phases & timeline (plausible):
- Phase 0 (2–3 weeks): PRD + design spec, ADRs for assignment determinism and metrics schema, design prototypes.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): Backend primitives (policy/assignment, exposure logs), telemetry schema + pipelines, basic Console CRUD UI, internal dogfood.
- Phase 2 (3–5 weeks): Experiment results UI, statistical comparisons, dashboards/alerts, eval harness attachment, beta with 2–3 design partners.
- Phase 3 (2–4 weeks): Hardening, runbooks, docs, GA criteria, staged rollout across regions/tiers.

Primary deliverables:
- Control-plane support for route-level experiment configs and deterministic assignment.
- Telemetry additions for experiment exposures and per-variant metrics aggregation.
- Console workflows (create, validate, start/stop, rollback) and results dashboards.
- Evals integration (attach suites, display offline quality deltas).
- Operational readiness: SLO expectations, alerting, audit events, incident playbooks.

Constraints & considerations:
- Assignment must be stable and privacy-safe (hashing on tenant/user/request fields with documented semantics).
- Metric collection must be low-overhead and avoid high-cardinality explosions.
- Must work across Hosted and Dedicated; Private support may be gated or follow-on.
- Clear separation between experimentation (measurement) and routing fallbacks (reliability), with well-defined precedence rules.

files.description: PRD: user problems, target personas, scope, success metrics (adoption + reliability), tier gating (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and GA criteria for route-level A/B testing in Console.
End-to-end design spec covering Console UX flows (create experiment, validate config, start/stop, rollback), permissions, audit views, and results reporting requirements.
ADR choosing deterministic assignment strategy (hash inputs, stickiness duration, bucketing), handling of retries/streaming, and compatibility with existing routing/fallback policies.
ADR defining exposure event format, PII constraints, sampling policy, and retention/access rules for experiment logs used in Console reporting.
Standardized metrics/events schema for experiments: required fields, cardinality rules, latency/cost metrics, and guidance for adding new metrics without breaking dashboards.
Service overview for the control-plane component that evaluates policies and returns experiment assignments; APIs, data model, failure modes, and ownership.
Runbook for disabling an experiment quickly, rolling back traffic splits, verifying metrics recovery, and coordinating comms with Support/CS.
SLO expectations and guardrails for running experiments (max allowed latency regression, error-rate thresholds, alert routing, and automation hooks for rollback).
Design for attaching eval suites to an A/B experiment, computing quality deltas, and displaying results (including statistical tests and confidence intervals).
Internal-facing guidance for Solutions/DevEx on how customers should structure routes, what telemetry to expect, and troubleshooting common misconfigurations.
Audit logging spec: events emitted for create/update/start/stop/rollback, required fields, and how auditors can reconstruct experiment history.
Release notes draft for beta launch: feature summary, limitations, known issues, migration notes, and links to runbooks/support playbooks.
Working PRD draft with open questions, tier gating debate, pricing thoughts, and early customer quotes/requests.
Design/eng collaboration notes on Console screens, edge cases (paused experiments, overlapping rollouts), and copy/terminology alternatives.
Spike write-up exploring candidate hash keys (tenant_id, api_key_id, user_id header), stickiness trade-offs, and replayability for debugging.
Checklist and analysis of metric dimensions, proposed cardinality limits, and instrumentation plan to avoid high-cardinality blowups.
Stats plan for comparing variants on eval scores (tests, multiple comparisons handling, minimum sample size guidance) and how to explain results in Console.
Weekly project notes: status, blockers, decisions pending, links to Linear issues and PRs, and next-week plan.
Weekly project notes focusing on beta readiness, instrumentation gaps, and design feedback from internal dogfood.
Spreadsheet-style table tracking beta partners, routes under test, split %, start dates, success metrics, and issues encountered.
Slides with proposed dashboard layouts for experiment results: latency/cost/error comparisons, exposure volume, and drill-downs.
PM ticket to finalize PRD, define beta/GA gating, and align internal launch checklist with SRE/security requirements.
Design issue for the create/validate/start flow; includes prototype links, copy review, and edge-case handling (overlapping rollouts).
Design issue for results dashboard components (variant comparison, confidence indicators, filtering by region/route) and accessibility considerations.
Implement policy evaluation changes to support experiment configs and deterministic assignment; includes acceptance criteria and perf budget.
Add exposure events to telemetry pipeline; define schema, sampling rules, backfill plan, and validation tests.
Console backend APIs for experiment CRUD, validation, start/stop, and rollback; includes authz checks and audit log hooks.
Aggregation jobs/materialized views for per-variant metrics (latency, cost, errors) and query patterns needed by the UI.
Create dashboards and alert rules tied to experiment IDs; integrate guardrail alerts with rollback runbook.
Evals integration work: link eval suites to an experiment, compute deltas, and surface in Console; includes data contracts and tests.
Security review checklist: audit event coverage, permission model, and potential abuse scenarios (traffic shifting) with mitigations.
Plan beta rollout across regions/tiers using feature flags; includes monitoring checklist and rollback triggers.
